standard_prerequisites.name: The simplicial-site situation and ringed morphisms of simplicial sites
standard_prerequisites.use: Statement lines 1604-1612: O, O' sheaves of rings on the total sites; (h, h^sharp) a morphism between simplicial sites as in the remark.

standard_prerequisites.name: The sheaf-level morphism of total topoi
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1635-1637: the morphism of topoi h_total and the commutative diagrams at the sheaf level, from which the ringed version follows.

standard_prerequisites.name: The ringed component restrictions g_n
standard_prerequisites.use: Statement lines 1629-1631 and proof lines 1637-1644: g_n and g'_n as morphisms of ringed topoi; the definition of h_n^sharp uses their ring identifications.

core_obligations: The ringed morphism (proof lines 1635-1644): the topos morphism and commutative diagrams follow from the sheaf-level lemma and the modules restriction lemma by keeping track of the sheaves of rings; to define h_n as a morphism of ringed topoi one sets h_n^sharp = g_n^{-1}h^sharp : g_n^{-1}h_{total}^{-1}O' -> g_n^{-1}O, which makes sense because g_n^{-1}h_{total}^{-1}O' = h_n^{-1}(g'_n)^{-1}O' = h_n^{-1}O'_n and g_n^{-1}O = O_n.

The compatibility identity (lines 1645-1653): g_n^*F = g_n^{-1}F for a sheaf of O-modules F (and similarly for g'_n), which explains why the identity (g'_n)^* h_{total,*} = h_{n,*} g_n^* of functors Mod(O) -> Mod(O'_n) follows from the corresponding sheaf-level statement of the morphism lemma.
proof_roadmap: Lift the sheaf-level morphism h_total to the ringed topoi.
Define the component maps h_n^sharp and check the ring identifications making them morphisms of ringed topoi.
Derive the pushforward compatibility from the sheaf-level identity via g_n^* = g_n^{-1} on modules.
difficulty_reason: Infrastructure lemma (statement 1603-1633, proof 1635-1653): lifts the sheaf-level morphism of simplicial sites to the ringed setting - the only new datum is the component map h_n^sharp, defined and checked via the ring identifications, and the pushforward compatibility follows from the sheaf-level identity via g_n^* = g_n^{-1} on modules; no verification is omitted. H2: ringed bookkeeping over the established sheaf-level morphism.
